task: I want a report (the folder must be written in the appropriate path/location) about all the possible edge cases that can happen during the member transfer process.

findings.title: P-05 describes an impossible scenario
findings.detail: The report claims id=0 and is_member=True can coexist, causing _peer_of() to return None and degrade checks to UNKNOWN. This is impossible: ChatInviteAlready (which sets is_member=True) returns the actual chat entity with a real ID via _entity_to_resolved(). The id=0 + is_member=True state never exists. The edge case entry should be corrected or removed.

findings.title: J-05 describes wrong behavior for unparseable limited_until
findings.detail: The report says an account with status=limited but unparseable limited_until is 'treated as active.' The actual code (job_manager.py:143-144) rejects job creation with MSG_ACCOUNT_LIMITED when _parse_limited_until returns None. The account is safely rejected, not treated as active. The severity rating of 'Potential bug' should be downgraded since the behavior is safe.

findings.title: T-09 incorrectly claims FloodWait retries during dest fetch
findings.detail: The report states FloodWait during dest member iteration 'retries after sleep' if attempt < 2. In reality, _handle_fetch_error classifies FloodWaitError as FLOOD_WAIT with retryable=False (errors.py:118), so it immediately aborts without retry. Only TRANSIENT errors are retryable in the fetch path. The trigger-and-behavior description is factually wrong.

findings.title: Missing edge case: ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED during invite
findings.detail: UserIsBlockedError maps to ErrorKind.ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED (errors.py:190-194) and aborts the job without per-member handling. This is not documented in T-01 through T-04.

findings.title: Missing edge case: INPUT_INVALID during invite
findings.detail: PeerIdInvalidError, UserIdInvalidError, ChatIdInvalidError, InviteHashExpiredError, and InviteHashInvalidError all map to ErrorKind.INPUT_INVALID (errors.py:196-206) and abort the job. These are not documented in the transfer engine section.

findings.title: Missing edge case: user settings bypass config validation
findings.detail: UserSettings.set() (settings.py:41-43) stores raw ints with no bounds checking. A user can set invite_delay_seconds=-5 or flood_wait_max_seconds=0 at the settings layer, bypassing the config-level ge=0 constraints. CFG-10 partially addresses this but understates the scope.

findings.title: Severity ratings need adjustment
findings.detail: J-05 should be downgraded from Medium to Low (safe rejection, not a bypass). DB-04 (audit log failure propagation) should be upgraded from a note to Medium severity since an unhandled exception in _finalize could prevent account slot cleanup.
